title: Allocator war findings waterline
purpose: Preserve the first source-custodied allocator-war findings waterline from SSC-H01 Wave 01 without converting bounded observations, controls, open denominators, or refused inferences into a complete compact, racial-order, prevalence, coordination, common-purpose, actor-edge, or publication finding.
working_definition: The allocator war is a contest over who may define merit, eligibility, admissible evidence, the option universe, public support, residual rights, and correction. The current waterline tests transfers of those functions. It does not presume that every DEI program is lawful or effective, that every strategic-capital program is captured, or that public preference itself establishes a racial order.

finding_classes.label: Anti-DEI allocator transfer
finding_classes.supported_statement: Five exact executive or personnel instruments changed selector authority, evaluative criteria, or the admissibility of DEI, affirmative-action, disparate-impact, contractor, or Foreign Service evidence.
finding_classes.evidence_ceiling: The records support bounded allocator and admissibility transfer. They do not establish that every displaced program was lawful or effective, a complete racial order, prevalence, or practical correction monopoly.
next_required_records: complete affected-program and affected-person denominators
implementation, enforcement, appeal, and outcome records
practical timing, cost, durability, and effectiveness of correction

finding_classes.label: Public conversion into selected private capacity
finding_classes.supported_statement: A named Defense Production Act award joined public funding and validation to selected private production capacity.
finding_classes.evidence_ceiling: The record does not establish the complete supplier universe, award terms, comparative performance, substitution capacity, or public recovery.
next_required_records: complete applicant and supplier denominator
evaluation and award terms
milestones, performance, failure, substitution, and public recovery

finding_classes.label: Effective independent counterpower controls
finding_classes.supported_statement: Independent judicial and procurement-review bodies preserved evidence and created a binding correction pathway without predetermining the underlying merits.
finding_classes.evidence_ceiling: The controls demonstrate that correction can work at a bounded gate. They do not establish system-wide adequacy or final downstream compliance.
next_required_records: final remand or corrective-action outcomes
cost, delay, durability, and recurrence after correction

finding_classes.label: Ordinary industrial-policy controls
finding_classes.supported_statement: Named strategic-finance and CHIPS instruments show that purposive public selection can coexist with disclosed instruments, due diligence or milestones, and formal oversight.
finding_classes.evidence_ceiling: The controls prevent public preference, national-security framing, or private benefit from becoming automatic capture findings. Final performance and recovery remain open.
next_required_records: complete applicant denominators
operative agreements and disbursement records
performance, enforcement, repayment, clawback, and public recovery

finding_classes.label: Open selector and strategic-capital denominators
finding_classes.supported_statement: NatSec100, SBIC Critical Technologies, and Office of Strategic Capital selection surfaces are source-addressable and partially denominator-bounded.
finding_classes.evidence_ceiling: Selected rosters, aggregate applicant counts, named instruments, and methodology categories do not supply complete preselection universes, rejected rows, exact scoring, terms, performance, failure, or recovery.
next_required_records: complete candidate and applicant universes
all rejected, ineligible, withdrawn, and failed rows
exact scoring, committee, FOCI, underwriting, and adverse-decision custody
commitment, draw, disbursement, performance, default, repayment, and public-recovery records
bounded later capital, award, deployment, failure, and nonaward joins

finding_classes.label: Stronger merit-circularity inference refused
finding_classes.supported_statement: A first-party narrative linked public support, capacity growth, supplier status, and later contracts.
finding_classes.refused_statement: The record does not establish that public conversion caused the later success, that the selected company displaced comparable alternatives, or that retained private value became proof of intrinsic merit.
next_required_records: official award instrument and exact terms
complete comparator and supplier universe
independent performance and failure evidence
public contribution, rights, recovery, and residual-value chronology

cross_class_findings.label: Allocator authority changed rather than disappeared
cross_class_findings.statement: The observed instruments support a bounded distinction between abolishing selection and reallocating selector, evidentiary, conversion, and correction authority.
cross_class_findings.limit: The current denominator does not establish prevalence, a complete preference monopoly, or one common purpose across the political, administrative, and defense-capital surfaces.

cross_class_findings.label: Public preference is not the discriminator
cross_class_findings.statement: The discriminator is whether criteria, denominators, alternative evidence, public and private risk, residual rights, and binding correction remain inspectable and practically contestable.
cross_class_findings.limit: A lawful or well-structured control does not validate every policy in its class, and an incomplete denominator does not prove capture.

promotion_requirements: second-party review of the fourteen bounded packets
adjudication under the SSC four-gate contract
execution of the untested conditional-incorporation, appointments, personnel-routing, foreclosure, and affected-party lanes
complete selected and rejected denominators for the relevant allocator
observed consequence and practical correction topology
separate authority for any racial-order, prevalence, coordination, common-purpose, graph, or publication finding
